articles.title: How to prepare your startup for a Series A raise in 2026
articles.snippet: How to prepare your startup for a Series A raise in 2026 Techli
articles.text:
For many startup founders, reaching the Series A stage is one of the most demanding transitions in building a company. The early excitement of launching a product, securing the first customers and celebrating initial revenue gradually gives way to a different set of responsibilities: proving to investors that the company is moving from experimental and early-stage products to a sustainable business that can generate revenue on repeatable basis.
Fewer and fewer founders are clearing that bar. Only 24% of U.S. startups that raised a seed round of $1 million USD or more in 2023 have since raised further funding, for example, according to Crunchbase data, down from a typical rate of 55% or higher for companies that raised seed rounds through 2020.
This is particularly relevant in 2026. U.S. startups raised approximately $42 billion in Series A funding through October, representing a 60% increase year over year, per Crunchbase. Yet, the number of deals has stayed roughly flat, meaning investors are writing bigger checks to a small group of companies that show the strongest potential for growth.
Revenue growth must be repeatable
While a strong revenue figure can help get a meeting with investors, it is not enough to secure funding. Some investors are writing larger checks at the seed stage, while others wait for later rounds of funding when there is more evidence of traction.
Here, founders must be able to prove that their early customers can be converted into a sustainable source of revenue for the company.
For Series A, investors are looking to understand how the company acquires customers, how long it takes to close a deal, and if growth can continue to scale with acquisition costs that are less than or equal to revenue growth, according to venture firm CRV. This means founders should prepare to discuss customer acquisition costs, gross margins, sales cycles, and cash burn for the company, in addition to revenue.
Retention is also critical. Whether the product solves a long-term problem for the customer and if the customer continues to use the product on a regular basis are key indicators of a startup’s success. Cohort analysis of customers, churn rates and net revenue retention (NRR) are key metrics that indicate whether there is sustainable demand for a startup’s product.
Carta’s Series A guidance , for example, outlines the key measures of product-market fit, revenue traction, healthy unit economics and a financial roadmap that are required for Series A funding.
Make the financial plan withstand scrutiny
A Series A financial model should connect the founders’ projections to operating evidence. Hiring plans, sales capacity, conversion rates, pricing, infrastructure costs and sales cycles can all support the founders’ forecast. Founders should explain their assumptions and prepare both a base-case and a downside scenario.
A big part of the Series A pitch is explaining what the funding will be used for; whether that is to hit a certain revenue number, enter a new market, or expand sales, the funding must be used to help the company reach measurable goals.
As the founder, you need to pull together your financial statements, current cap table, customer and revenue data, retention metrics, current contracts, and product metrics before going to market for Series A.
In sum, be ready to explain your customer concentration, churn, and delayed deals, as well as your growth.

Gasgoo Munich- Gasgoo Embodied Intelligence has learned that Fortsense has officially closed a Series C4 funding round exceeding 400 million yuan. The round drew a mix of industrial capital from listed companies and specialized investment firms, including Senter Electronic, Jingce Electronic, SINOWISDOM, Huining Investment, Xingyin Financial Asset Investment, Qingke Capital, and the China-Europe New Energy Vehicle Fund. The fresh capital will primarily fund the technical iteration and commercial rollout of its physical AI spatial perception chips.
Image Source: Fortsense
As autonomous driving shifts from "passive perception" to "active understanding," spatial perception is emerging as a critical layer of infrastructure for the safe operation of physical AI. Leveraging its in-house SPAD chips and all-solid-state optical scanning technology, Fortsense is developing a single-chip RGBD solution. The architecture natively fuses color imagery with depth data on a single chip, fundamentally eliminating the latency and calibration errors typical of traditional multi-sensor setups that pair cameras with LiDAR.
On the commercialization front, the company's solid-state LiDAR SPAD chips have already entered automotive-grade mass production as original equipment for major automakers, with cumulative shipments surpassing 1 million units. Its integrated RGBD chip is slated for commercialization in 2027, targeting next-generation spatial perception applications across smart vehicles, embodied AI, and industrial intelligence. SINOWISDOM noted that as the physical AI sector accelerates, spatial perception chips are poised to see substantially broader market demand.

Soket AI Raises $4 Mn From Bajaj Finance And Pennant For On-Premise LLMs
Soket AI, a Bengaluru-based frontier AI lab building indigenous large language models under the IndiaAI Mission, has raised nearly $4 million from Bajaj Finance and Pennant Technologies.
Bajaj Finance invested about $2 million through Bajaj Finserv Intelligence, the group’s applied research initiative. Pennant Technologies, a lending software company in which Bajaj Finance holds a stake, put in another $2 million. India Accelerator and Finvolve also invested undisclosed amounts.
What the Money Is For
The round is not a general purpose cheque. It is a strategic investment by a lender that wants models it can run inside its own walls.
Read More: Boba Bhai Raises $18 Mn Series B From Left Lane, BIG Capital And Titan Capital
The Soket AI pitch is that its models can be deployed on an organisation’s own infrastructure, including on-premises environments. Trained and run at lower cost than frontier alternatives.
Read More: Style Union Raises Rs 485 Cr Series E Led By Venturi Partners To Expand Beyond South India
For a non-banking finance company handling millions of customer records, that is the whole argument. Data residency and control are procurement conditions, not preferences.
Why a Lender Wants Its Own Model
Financial services companies are testing AI across lending, customer service, risk assessment and cybersecurity.
Each of those use cases touches sensitive customer data. Raises a question that no API provider answers well: where does the data go, and who controls the infrastructure the model runs on.
“The next phase of AI will be defined by outcomes delivered at sustainable cost,” said Rajeev Jain of Bajaj Finance, adding that efficient reasoning-led models can make advanced AI economically viable for financial services while running securely within its own infrastructure.
Sanjiv Bajaj, chairman and managing director of Bajaj Finserv, said the margin for error must be minimal as AI becomes part of critical information infrastructure. Framed the investment as backing indigenous research.
The IndiaAI Mission Angle
Soket AI, a Bengaluru lab, is one of the startups building models under the government’s IndiaAI Mission. Subsidises compute and supports domestic foundation models.
For Soket AI, that backing gives a young lab access to GPU capacity it could not otherwise afford. It gives government buyers a reason to consider the model seriously.
It also creates an expectation. A mission-backed lab is expected to publish benchmarks and demonstrate that its models handle Indian languages and Indian data, not just English benchmarks.
The Competitive Problem
For Soket AI, every Indian enterprise evaluating a domestic model compares it with a global one that is usually better on general reasoning.
For Soket AI, the domestic pitch has to be narrower and more concrete: cheaper inference, control over where data sits. Support that answers within a day.
Soket AI’s claim of efficient reasoning-led models is aimed exactly at that gap, since inference cost is what makes a model viable at scale inside a bank.
The cost argument is the one that survives scrutiny. A bank runs a model on millions of documents a year, so a small difference in cost per token becomes a budget line.

articles.text:
Oliver Wyman To Acquire Synpulse To Expand Financial Services Technology And AI Capabilities
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:36 PM
Oliver Wyman To Acquire Synpulse To Expand Financial Services Technology And AI Capabilities
Oliver Wyman, Marsh’s management consulting business, has agreed to acquire Synpulse, a technology consulting and AI platform company serving banks, insurers, wealth managers and other financial services organizations.
The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The acquisition will bring together Oliver Wyman’s strategy consulting capabilities and Synpulse’s technology implementation and AI engineering expertise. The businesses have already worked together through combined teams on multiple client transformation projects.
Financial institutions are adapting to advances in technology, data and AI alongside changing business models. The combination is intended to help clients manage projects across that transition, connecting strategic planning with technology implementation and execution.
Founded in 1996, Synpulse helps financial institutions modernize legacy systems, improve operations and respond to changing customer needs. Its work includes responsible AI strategy and digital ecosystem transformation, supporting clients as they introduce products, simplify processes and develop more personalized customer experiences.
Following the acquisition, Synpulse’s approximately 1,200 employees will continue operating from offices across North America, Europe and Asia.
For Oliver Wyman, the transaction adds technology consulting and engineering resources focused on financial services. For Synpulse, the combination provides greater scale to support clients throughout their digital and AI transformation programs.
The companies also see opportunities to expand across markets, pursue larger and more complex transformation assignments, and strengthen investment in AI and technology capabilities.
Their existing collaboration provides a foundation for the combination, with teams already delivering projects that span strategy and implementation. The acquisition would formalize that relationship and broaden the capabilities available to their financial services clients.
KEY QUOTES
“Our clients don’t separate strategy from technology and execution—they need great ideas to deliver real change. Synpulse brings exceptional technology consulting and AI engineering capabilities, deep financial services expertise and a track record of delivering complex enterprise change. Together, we will deliver a winning combination of talent and technology to help clients achieve their biggest ambitions.”
Ted Moynihan, President And CEO Of Oliver Wyman And Marsh Management Consulting
“Since our founding in 1996, Synpulse has built a strong position as a trusted partner to financial institutions in their digital transformations. Working alongside Oliver Wyman will enable us to support our clients across the entire digital and AI transformation journey, from strategy through implementation and execution. It gives us greater scale to deepen the value we bring to our clients.”
Konrad Niggli, Co-CEO Of Synpulse
